hints: All flight lengths are positive, so Dijkstra's algorithm applies.
Keep the best known distance to each city and use a min-priority queue to process the smallest tentative distance.
Ignore stale queue entries after a shorter route has already been found.
analogy: Always expand the currently cheapest known route; positive lengths ensure a finalized route cannot later improve.
example: If 1->3 costs 2 and 3->2 costs 3, city 2 has route length 5 even if direct alternatives cost more.
algorithm: Initialize dist[1]=0. Pop (distance,u), relax each directed edge u->v with positive weight, and push improved distances.
correctness: When u is removed with the smallest tentative distance, any route that could improve it would have to pass through a vertex with no larger distance already processed, so its distance is final.
complexity: O((n+m) log n) time and O(n+m) space.
